newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK wants PLA to replace British in dragonboat gala.
newsitem.headline: HK wants PLA to replace British in dragonboat gala.

text.p: Organisers of Hong Kong's annual dragon boat races plan to invite People's Liberation Army garrison troops to join the fun next year, as the departing British garrison has done for years.

With only 21 days to Hong Kong's return to the Chinese rule, local community groups said on Tuesday they want the PLA forces here to take part in the festivities that pit teams of beefy rowers in giant boats against each other.

Britain is handing back Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30, and the Black Watch regiment is leaving. British soldiers have traditionally been active in the dragon boat races in Stanley village, which took place on Monday.
"I'm pretty sure the residents' group in Stanley will formally invite the PLA," said Joop Litmaath, an organiser of Monday's traditional long-prowed boating contest in Stanley.
"We are not a political organisation, why should we not ask the PLA to take part next year?"
More than 120 Western expatriate and local teams joined in Monday's Stanley races, Litmaath. Hundreds more contests took place at the same time in other Hong Kong communities.
